title: PHYSICS COMPOSITION -- five bouncing balls play pitches and write a piano roll

sections.heading: USING IT
lines: Needs the Dada and bach packages. Turn on audio, then the Play / Stop toggle.
Five coloured balls bounce inside a V-shaped funnel. Every bounce plays a note.
Where a ball hits (left to right) sets its pitch, from Min Hz up to Max Hz (default 55-4186).
Pitch is continuous -- no scale -- and the note is panned by the same left/right position.
Harder hits play louder. Each ball has its own timbre (a different upper partial).
Speed (playstep ms): lower = faster simulation. Ball size: ball radius in pixels.
Reset: puts the five balls back at their start and clears the roll.
Clear notation: clears the bach.roll only; the balls keep moving.
The two gain~ faders set the left and right master level.

sections.heading: HOW IT WORKS
lines: dada.bounce is used only as a physics engine; its bounce data goes out on send ball-event.
p voice-1 to p voice-5 each pick their ball and map hit x to frequency on a log sweep.
Each voice is two cycle~ oscillators with an adsr~ envelope and constant-power pan.
Each note is also sent to bach.roll (onset, pitch in midicents, 500 ms, velocity).
The voices are summed, then limi~ protects the output before dac~ 1 2.
